pillar_reactions.evidence: Confirmed without questions — 'Does that align with like what you're looking for?' / 'Yeah. Yeah, exactly.' He had already framed the modality himself as the answer to his stated problem: 'I want a more holistic approach to working out. I just want to be more nimble... rather than just your typical push-pull-press kind of ordeal.' The mobility half was the piece he cared most about and he had named the specific targets — hips, knees, ankles — before it was presented.

Pre-demoted by the rep — 'you're kind of already there, which is a good thing... it's probably going to be the least focused' — and the prospect had already established an animal-based approach when in a training cycle. No questions and no resistance. Notably his one nutrition-adjacent goal, breaking a heavy caffeine reliance, was elicited earlier and never connected to this pillar.

The pillar that sold him, and he said so unprompted when asked what mattered: 'the biggest thing for me is just, is the accountability.' He then framed the purchase around it: 'I want to make this a lifestyle thing rather than just on and off and do it here and there. So that's really the change I want to make.' The rep's Ferrari metaphor — 'we can be the Ferrari to get you around the racetrack, you've still got to drive the car, but we also want to make sure you know exactly how to drive that car and we make sure you get in the car too' — landed cleanly.

anchors.raw: I would say probably 70% of our clients are business owners. So we're always helping you frame it so you can write it off as well... for a guy I signed up yesterday we framed it as safety and injury prevention program for example. So we can help you write it off as taxes so it's almost free.
anchors.note: The most consequential anchor in the batch, because of when it was placed — roughly ninety seconds before the price. The prospect adopted it as his decision criterion within two minutes of hearing the number: 'if I can swing it with through the business as a write-off, that's obviously more definitely doable.' It converted a $6,000 decision he could make into one his accountant has to approve, which is why this call is a follow-up rather than a close.

anchors.raw: I mean, it's definitely a lot pricier than I was anticipating. No, not going to lie there.
anchors.note: A clean, honest statement of a gap between expectation and price with no attempt to negotiate it — consistent with an optimiser rather than a bargain hunter. He moved straight from the reaction to asking about the contract, which is buying behaviour.

anchors.raw: I did maybe some of those free workout stuff before, the past, maybe a year ago. And it was, I feel like it was good stuff.
anchors.note: He has already tried the free version and rated it. The paid offer therefore has to justify itself on tailoring and accountability rather than on content, which is exactly where he placed his own value — but nobody made that contrast explicitly.

anchors.raw: I was very well versed in like bodybuilding and all that. I went hard at it years ago... So I know my way around, you know, movements and whatnot
anchors.note: He can already programme and execute training; what he cannot do is stay consistent. That makes the accountability pillar the only genuinely non-substitutable part of the offer for him, and it is the part he responded to.

unmet_demand.want: A written proposal with the numbers laid out, explicitly to take to his accountant — 'I want to see basically what we went over with call written down with a price number'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep described a two-page agreement as a post-purchase formality rather than a pre-purchase document, and nothing had been sent when the recording ended. The prospect needs collateral to hold a conversation the rep has made central to the sale, and there is apparently none.

unmet_demand.want: Help breaking a heavy caffeine reliance — 'I do rely on caffeine a lot. And that's one of those things I want to break as well.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Elicited by a good question and then never referenced again. The nutrition and energy pillar plausibly addresses it, and nobody connected the two, so a stated goal went into the decision unanswered.

unmet_demand.want: Better sleep — seven hours which he knows is not optimal, with three children and a business
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only call in the batch where sleep was asked, and the answer was not used. Sleep is tracked in the app per the rep's own description, but was never presented as something the programme improves or monitors.
